text:
alex: hey runtime team :wave: I'm Alex, just joined today. Trying to build the runtime from source on Ubuntu 22.04 and hit a linker error on cublas. Followed the dev docs and dev container steps.
alex: build finishes cmake/ninja but link fails:
alex: ```
/usr/bin/ld: CMakeFiles/runtime.dir/src/kernels/cuda_kernels.o: in function `init_cublas':
undefined reference to `cublasCreate_v2'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
alex: nvcc --version: 12.2, nvidia-smi shows Driver Version: 525.85.10, CUDA toolkit installed at /usr/local/cuda-12.2
maria: welcome Alex! :wave: quick checks: is libcublas present in your lib64? try `ldd build/runtime | grep cublas` and also ensure LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64 before cmake.
tyler: also run `git submodule update --init --recursive` — our thirdparty/cublas wrappers sometimes don't get pulled in and that causes missing symbols.
alex: ran ldd and see `libcublas.so.12 => not found` so that explains it.
morgan: yep. There are two common fixes: 1) install the matching CUDA toolkit package which populates the targets/x86_64-linux/lib/*.so* and sets symlinks, or 2) create a symlink if you know the exact file. Eg:
```
sudo ln -s /usr/local/cuda-12.2/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/libcublas.so /usr/local/cuda-12.2/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/libcublas.so.12
sudo ldconfig
```
But installing the toolkit deb is preferred so all deps are correct.
maria: additionally, make sure you set cmake flags so the rpath is baked in: `-DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64` or set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in your build environment. And double-check `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` matches the GPU.
dev-bot: dev-image-bot: CI uses drivers >= 525 and CUDA 12.1 in the default dev images. See https://redwood.dev/dev-env for recommended local dev setup.
alex: tried symlink + ldconfig then re-ran `cmake --build build --clean-first` and the link moved past cublas but now fails on a missing cudnn symbol. sigh.
tyler: for cudnn either install the cuDNN tarball into the toolkit targets dir or use the deb package. If you're doing ad-hoc symlinks you can get into subtle mismatches.
alex: small question — do we have a supported dev container for mac intel or M1? I'm on an M1 laptop.\
morgan: we don't have M1 containers officially. Recommended: use a linux VM in GCP or request a remote dev box from infra. Ping infra in #eng-infra and mention you need GPU access.
alex: thanks, everyone. I'll try the toolkit install on a linux VM and update here. :thumbsup:
tyler: ping me if you need credentials for the remote box or want me to pair on the build.
alex: will do — appreciate the quick replies!
